title: Oath of Kraków vs Martyrs' Legion
lede:
Martyrs' Legion won 33-28 on Victory Points at the end of Battle Round 5, from 18-7 down after Round 2.

The Oath of Kraków took all three objectives in Round 1, then lost Tadeusz Kosciuszko, the Silesian Hammerguards and all three Commonwealth Fusiliers in two rounds, to the Archistrategos, his Knight-Apostle Squad and two Covenant Levies; the Legion held the left from Round 3 and the centre from Round 4, and hit the 10 VP round cap twice.
result_line: Martyrs' Legion win 33-28 on Victory Points in Battle Round 5
deployment: Central Faceoff on CROSSROADS, three objectives on row 7: the 3 VP centre at (7,7) and the 2 VP flanks at (1,7) and (13,7). The Oath of Kraków set up along row 12 in front of its HQ at (7,13): Commonwealth Fusiliers 3 (3,12), Consecrated Hussars 1 (4,12) and Commonwealth Fusiliers 2 (5,12) on the left, the Tri-Banner Chaplain with Commonwealth Fusiliers 1 (9,12), Tadeusz Kosciuszko with the Silesian Hammerguards (10,12) and Consecrated Hussars 2 (11,12) on the right. Martyrs' Legion set up on row 2 in front of its HQ at (7,1): the Staurotheke War-Shrine (3,2), Covenant Levies 2 (4,2), the Archistrategos with the Knight-Apostle Squad (6,2), Covenant Levies 3 (7,2), the Cantor-Preceptor with Covenant Levies 1 (9,2), Covenant Levies 4 (10,2) and the Golgothic Paladins (11,2); its Round 1 Troop Requisition added a fifth Covenant Levies at (8,2). The Oath had the faster wings, the Legion the heavier melee in the middle and five cheap ten-model squads. The Oath had Priority every round (fewer units on the battlefield).

1.title: The Oath on all three objectives

feed.text: Primaries revealed: IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS for the Oath, LEAD FROM THE FRONT for the Legion. Secondaries kept: TAKE UP THE GAUNTLET, for which the Legion named the left objective, and BAR THE GATES. The Legion spent 3 CP on Troop Requisition (Covenant Levies at 8,2).

Consecrated Hussars 1 rode to 2,8 on the left and Consecrated Hussars 2 to 13,7 on the right. Kosciuszko with the Hammerguards (8,8), the Chaplain with Commonwealth Fusiliers 1 (7,8) and Commonwealth Fusiliers 3 (6,8) took the centre. The Legion met them on row 6: the Golgothic Paladins at 8,6, the Knight-Apostle Squad with the Archistrategos at 9,6, and three Covenant Levies around 6,6 to 7,5.

One attack: the Knight-Apostle Squad shot at Kosciuszko for 2 on the Hammerguards, with the Legion's Providence Miracle (Taxiarch of Miracles kept it unspent) against the Oath's Go to Ground (1 CP). PRAYING paid the Legion 16 Mana and the Oath 8.

The Oath scored all three objectives, the centre on OC 43 vs 26 and both flanks on OC 6 vs 0 (7 VP), and TAKE UP THE GAUNTLET for 3: the round's 10 VP. BAR THE GATES completed for the Legion, +2. 10-2.
No HQ Commands were issued. Secondaries kept: TERRITORIAL SUPERIORITY and OBJECTIVE RELAY.

Covenant Levies 3 took 4 HP of Fusilier Overwatch walking to 5,6, and Covenant Levies 4 traded Overwatch with Consecrated Hussars 2 on its way to 11,6. When the Knight-Apostle Squad charged, the Oath spent 3 CP on Countercharge: the Silesian Hammerguards and Kosciuszko charged the Archistrategos, the Knight-Apostle Squad, the Golgothic Paladins and the Covenant Levies at 8,7, and the Knight-Apostle Squad's charge was canceled.

The Tri-Banner Chaplain cast Ruthenian Field Icon on the Hammerguards (3 Mana, a reroll) and the Cantor-Preceptor Agnus Dei on Covenant Levies 2 (6 Mana). The Archistrategos used Quis ut Deus? (+2 AR, +2 FR, +2 DMG, LETHAL) with the Exaltation Miracle and destroyed the Silesian Hammerguards. Covenant Levies 2 shot Commonwealth Fusiliers 3 to death (10). Kosciuszko attacked the Golgothic Paladins and lost 5; the Knight-Apostle Squad destroyed him and took ground to 8,7. Commonwealth Fusiliers 1 failed Morale.

The Legion took the centre on OC 32 vs 0 (3 VP) and LEAD FROM THE FRONT 2. The Oath held the left (OC 16 vs 0) and the right (OC 6 vs 0), 4 VP, IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS 1 and TERRITORIAL SUPERIORITY 3. 18-7.

3.title: The Fusiliers fall and the left goes to the Levies

feed.text: The Legion spent 3 CP on Troop Requisition (Covenant Levies #2 at 5,2) and 2 on Double Time for it; the Oath 2 CP on Rally Cry for Commonwealth Fusiliers 1. Secondaries kept: SECURE THE FLANKS and BREAK CONTACT.

Commonwealth Fusiliers 1 failed its Fall Back test and broke away in disorder to 10,9, losing two models. Consecrated Hussars 1 left the left objective for 6,8, and the Levies moved onto the left: Covenant Levies 3 to 2,6, with the Cantor-Preceptor's squad behind it at 3,7. The Golgothic Paladins charged Consecrated Hussars 1 and the Knight-Apostle Squad charged the Fusiliers and the Chaplain at 9,8. Covenant Levies 4 reached 12,6, inside the right objective's area.

The Cantor-Preceptor cast Agnus Dei on Covenant Levies 1 (6 Mana), which then shot Commonwealth Fusiliers 2 to death (10). The Knight-Apostle Squad destroyed Commonwealth Fusiliers 1 and the Archistrategos hit the Chaplain for 2. Consecrated Hussars 2 and Covenant Levies 4 traded 2 HP each.

The centre tied 6-6 on OC and 1-1 on units. The Legion took the left (OC 7 vs 0) and the right (OC 7 vs 4, Covenant Levies 4 over Consecrated Hussars 2), 4 VP, and LEAD FROM THE FRONT 2. The Oath scored only IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS 1. 19-13.

4.title: Lance of God's Wrath, and the Legion's capped round

feed.text: The Legion spent 3 CP on Double Time for Covenant Levies #2; the Oath held its 3 CP. Secondaries kept: DEEP REACH and TERRITORIAL SUPERIORITY.

Consecrated Hussars 2 charged Covenant Levies 4 at 12,7: Lance of God's Wrath took 13 HP (14 to 1) and Covenant Levies 4 died breaking away in disorder. The Knight-Apostle Squad left the 3 HP Chaplain, broke away in disorder (3 HP) and landed on the centre at 7,6. Covenant Levies 1 with the Cantor-Preceptor and Covenant Levies 2 walked into the Oath's half, to 4,10 and 4,9.

The Cantor-Preceptor cast Gloria on Covenant Levies 1 (4 Mana) and the Levies shot the Oath's HQ for 6 (8 to 2). The Chaplain's Bogurodzica on Consecrated Hussars 2 (2 Mana) changed nothing. The Golgothic Paladins put 3 into Consecrated Hussars 1.

The Legion held the centre (OC 15 vs 4) and the left (OC 7 vs 0), 5 VP, LEAD FROM THE FRONT 3 and TERRITORIAL SUPERIORITY 2: the round's 10 VP, with 1 VP of TERRITORIAL SUPERIORITY and both of BREAK CONTACT's withheld by the cap. The Oath retook the right (OC 4 vs 0), 2 VP, with IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS 1 and DEEP REACH 3. 25-23.

5.title: The Levies at the Oath's gate

feed.text: The Benediction Miracle healed the Knight-Apostle Squad 3. The Oath spent 5 CP on Troop Requisition (Commonwealth Fusiliers at 7,12), the Legion 3 on another (Covenant Levies #3 at 9,2, which did nothing). Secondaries kept: OBJECTIVE RELAY and FORWARD PRESENCE; SECURE THE FLANKS expired.

Covenant Levies 1 with the Cantor-Preceptor reached 6,12 and Covenant Levies 2 5,11, beside the Oath's HQ. The Knight-Apostle Squad charged the Chaplain again. The Staurotheke War-Shrine's charge failed.

The Tri-Banner Chaplain attacked the Knight-Apostle Squad and was destroyed. Covenant Levies 1 and the Cantor-Preceptor both used Capture on the HQ, making it CONTESTED, and FORWARD PRESENCE completed for 3 VP and 1 CP.

The Legion held the centre (OC 16 vs 4) and the left (OC 7 vs 0), 5 VP, and LEAD FROM THE FRONT 2, its third VP withheld by the cap. The Oath held the right and scored IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS 1. 28-33, the Legion past 30.

analysis.title: Why it went this way
analysis.html:
Where the VP came from

Martyrs' Legion scored 17 objective VP, all from Round 2 on: the centre in Rounds 2, 4 and 5, the left from Round 3 and the right once. LEAD FROM THE FRONT paid 9 (its CHARACTERs, the Archistrategos and the Cantor-Preceptor with their squads, in Objective Areas or the Oath's half every round from Round 2) and four secondaries 7. The 10 VP round cap held back 4 of its VP in Rounds 4 and 5. The Oath of Kraków scored 15 objective VP, 11 of them in Rounds 1 and 2, plus 9 from TAKE UP THE GAUNTLET, TERRITORIAL SUPERIORITY and DEEP REACH and 4 from IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS (1 a round from Round 2, when it never had more than three qualifying units outside its deployment zone).

{{chart:objectives}}

What the key units did

Consecrated Hussars 2 (48 RP) were the battle's top scorer, 12.8 VP: on the right objective in four of the five rounds, 19 damage, and Lance of God's Wrath's 13 HP that destroyed Covenant Levies 4 to take it back. Consecrated Hussars 1 held the left in Rounds 1 and 2 (7.8 VP, TAKE UP THE GAUNTLET). For the Legion, the Archistrategos (Quis ut Deus? and Exaltation) destroyed the Silesian Hammerguards and later the Chaplain, and the Knight-Apostle Squad took Kosciuszko and Commonwealth Fusiliers 1: 24 damage and 4 kills between the pair. Two 10 RP Covenant Levies with Antiphons did the rest of the killing, Commonwealth Fusiliers 2 and 3. Covenant Levies 3 took the left in Round 3 and held it to the end, 7.3 VP and 73.3 per 100 RP.

{{chart:attrition}}

What the Oath could not do

It could not hold the centre against the Legion's melee pair, and once the centre fell it had nothing to send back. It lost 156 RP, six units, to the Legion's 10: Kosciuszko, the Hammerguards, three Fusiliers and the Chaplain. From Round 3 its scoring units were the two Consecrated Hussars, and two units cannot hold three objectives. IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS, which pays for every two units outside the deployment zone, paid 1 a round once the infantry was gone.

{{chart:rp-trade}}

The AI, not the army

  • Round 2, Countercharge: the Oath's AI spent 3 CP to send the Silesian Hammerguards and Kosciuszko (95 RP) into four Legion units at once. The record counts it as paid off, because it canceled the Knight-Apostle Squad's charge, but both units were destroyed in that Action Phase and the centre went to the Legion.
  • Round 3, Consecrated Hussars 1 rode off the left objective to 6,8, where the Golgothic Paladins charged them. The left went to Covenant Levies 3 that round and stayed with the Legion to the end: 6 VP to the Legion, in a battle lost by 5.
  • Round 5, Troop Requisition: 5 CP for a 12 RP Commonwealth Fusiliers that scored 0.33 VP; the Legion's own Requisition that round did nothing.
  • On the Legion's side, the Staurotheke War-Shrine (30 RP) took no action in five rounds (its aura touched attacks), the Legion ended holding 26 Mana, and Covenant Levies 1 and the Cantor-Preceptor both spent an action on Capture of the same HQ, the second for nothing.

The army won the middle and the AI lost the left: the Legion's melee pair beats anything the Oath can put on the centre, but the Oath gave up the flank that would have kept the score level.

Against the first playing

The first playing went to Martyrs' Legion 35-16 in Round 4, on a 17 VP Round 4. The Oath then fielded a Rotmistrz with Consecrated Hussars 1; now it brought the Tri-Banner Chaplain with Commonwealth Fusiliers 1, a cheaper Kosciuszko (55 RP, was 65), and Consecrated Hussars at OC 2 a model, and it scored 10 in Round 1 instead of 8. The 10 VP round cap held the Legion to 10 in Rounds 4 and 5 (4 VP withheld) where the first playing let it score 17 in one round, and the battle went to a fifth round and a 5 VP margin instead of 19. The shape was the same: the Oath's centre destroyed by Round 3 and the Legion's Covenant Levies on the flanks.

closing_title: Lost in the middle, decided on the left
closing: The Oath's Hussars took the flanks and held the right to the end; its infantry and its hero died in the centre to the Archistrategos and his Knight-Apostles. When Consecrated Hussars 1 left the left objective, the Legion's cheap Levies had all the ground they needed.
